headline: PSX snapped its four-session losing streak — KSE-100 up ~465 points (+0.26%) to ~180,311 on reports the US and Iran agreed to extend their Hormuz ceasefire deadline; drawdown from the Jan ATH narrowed to ~4.9% (from ~5.1% yesterday), still well below the 10% deploy line. Portfolio value ~Rs 10.32M, P/L +Rs 438K (+4.43%), up from +4.10% yesterday — about a third of that gain (~Rs 32K) is fund NAVs finally catching up to reality rather than fresh market gains (see data-quality note below). No holding moved >2% today. Two genuinely new items this review: Meezan Bank declared an Rs 8/share interim dividend (board Aug 6) with a confirmed ex-date of Aug 18, 2026 — never previously flagged, so notifying now; Faysal Bank also declared Rs 1.50/share (same board date) but no ex-date is published yet. AVN's sell-half plan remains unexecuted, 10 days past the stated date.
market: KSE-100 reversed its four-day slide on Thu Aug 13, gaining 464.53 points (+0.26%) to close around 180,311.22 (intraday high 180,901.27) after reports that the US and Iran agreed to extend their Strait of Hormuz ceasefire deadline ahead of its 60-day expiry — easing the geopolitical risk premium that had driven Brent toward $90/bbl over the prior week. Energy and gas names led (Pakistan Oilfield, Mari Energies, SSGC +2.74%, SNGP +2.31%) on hopes of Pakistan-Iran petroleum/gas cooperation; none of these are Mali holdings, which is why the position-level moves were muted (largest today: FFL +1.7%, MUGHAL -0.8%, UPFL -1.0%, everything else under 1%). Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) narrowed to ~4.9% from ~5.1% yesterday — still well clear of the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve. SBP holds its policy rate at 11.5% (no new decision since the Jul 27 pause); no fresh IMF program news. EARNINGS/DIVIDENDS — checking upcoming dates for holdings turned up two items missed in prior reviews: Meezan Bank's board (Aug 6) approved an interim cash dividend of Rs 8.00/share (80%) for Q2 2026, on top of the Rs 7.50/share already paid this year (Rs 15.50/share total interim so far) — H1 PAT was Rs 48.9B, EPS Rs 27.15 (up from Rs 25.72), ROE 34.7%, NPL ratio 1.83%. Confirmed ex-date is Aug 18, 2026 (5 days out) — on 900 shares that's ~Rs 7,200 of dividend income; being a HOLD, no action needed beyond the calendar note, but flagging per the ex-dividend rule since this is its first confirmation. Faysal Bank's board (same Aug 6 meeting) approved Rs 1.50/share (15%) for Q2, adding to Rs 1.50/share already paid in Q1; H1 consolidated profit was roughly flat at Rs 10.35B (EPS Rs 6.82 vs Rs 6.87) — solid but not a growth story this half. No confirmed ex-date found yet for this one; will check again next review. AVN — no fresh company news found again; the stated 'Monday Aug 3 open' execution window for the sell-half plan is now 10 days gone with holdings still showing the full 24,500 shares. EFERT — nothing new since the Aug 5 briefing; still on WATCH into Q3. DATA QUALITY — the automated MUFAP fund-NAV fetch is STILL failing from GitHub Actions after yesterday's once-daily throttle fix (funds sat frozen at the same Aug 4 values through today's runs, funds_updated stayed null) — this disproves the over-scraping/rate-limit theory from yesterday. Tested curl against mufap.com.pk directly from a non-GitHub-Actions network this review: it succeeded immediately (HTTP 200, full data, matched all 8 funds), strongly suggesting mufap.com.pk's WAF is blocking GitHub Actions' shared runner IP ranges specifically (a common blanket policy against cloud-datacenter ASNs), not reacting to request frequency. Manually pulled live NAVs this review and corrected data/prices.json + data/history.json directly (ASSF 492.71, AKDISSF 110.571, NISIF 35.4121, NISF 25.1833, MIF 166.3348, AICF 102.6719, MICF 108.4795, all dated Aug 12-13 per MUFAP's own site) — fund P/L figures below are now accurate, not stale. The underlying scraper still needs a real fix next time someone can touch the code (e.g. routing through a proxy/relay outside GitHub's IP ranges, or a different data source) — the throttle alone will not fix an IP-range block.

actions.detail: −6.4% on cost (Rs 186.12 today; position unchanged at 2,600 shares). No fresh news since — second straight half of declining core earnings, worth testing against Q3 numbers before rotating out.
